title: The vanishing night
text: For most of history, night was genuinely dark, and the Milky Way was simply part of the sky. A 2016 study {{1}} that a third of humanity can no longer see it at all, and that in cities the whole heavens have been {{2}} to a pale orange dome. Astronomers complain, but the {{3}} extends far beyond stargazing. Migrating birds are {{4}} off course by glowing towers; sea-turtle hatchlings, which follow the brighter horizon towards the sea, crawl inland towards streetlights instead; insects {{5}} to their deaths around lamps in their billions, and studies of night-shift workers {{6}} the same blue-rich light to poor sleep and worse health. The good news is that light pollution is the rare environmental problem with an instant {{7}}: switch it off and the sky returns. Shielded fixtures that shine down instead of up, motion sensors instead of all-night brightness, warmer colours instead of blue-white — none of this {{8}} safety, and several cities have cut their light output by a third without any rise in crime or accidents. The stars, patient as ever, have simply been waiting to be let back in.

gaps.explanation: 'a study calculated that…' — worked out from data; circulate = spread round, captivate = fascinate.
'the heavens have been downgraded to a pale orange dome' — lowered to something poorer; demolish = tear down, devour = eat up.
'the damage extends far beyond stargazing' — the harm done; dosage = the size of a medicine dose, doctrine = a set of beliefs.
'birds are lured off course by glowing towers' — drawn irresistibly; loiter = stand about, lounge = relax.
'insects spiral to their deaths around lamps' — circle ever tighter downwards; spurt = gush suddenly.
'studies link the same light to poor sleep' — connect the two; brink = the edge, and 'blink to' is meaningless here.
'the rare environmental problem with an instant fix' — an immediate solution; fax is a machine, and failures and famines are not solutions.
'none of this compromises safety' — reduces it; corroborate = confirm with evidence, commemorate = honour a memory.
